messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "In all low-shot settings, our method VAGER+Voting consistently performs the best in both AUC and F1 metrics." -- cites: E1 (Section 4.2): quote "In all low-shot settings, our method VAGER+Voting consistently performs the best in both AUC and F1 metrics."
2. "LR performs the worst in 1-shot setting, which demonstrates the importance of generalization from base classes when the new class has very few samples." -- cites: E1 (Section 4.2): quote "LR performs the worst in 1-shot setting, which demonstrates the importance of generalization from base classes when the new class has very few samples."
3. "The performance of VAGER is worse than LR for the 'Bubble' class in the 1-shot binary classification setting." -- cites: E2 (Section Table 2): quote "Bubble 0.7455 0.7041"
4. "VAGER+Voting performs the best in all 5 groups, with promotion of around 2% of average top-1 accuracy." -- cites: E3 (Section 4.4): quote "Our VAGER+Voting performs the best in all 5 groups, with promotion of around 2% of average top-1 accuracy, which demonstrates that our method is robust whatever the novel classes are."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section 4.2, page 6): In this section, we evaluate how well the classiﬁers learned by our method and other baselines can perform in novel classes on binary classiﬁcation setting. The results are shown in Table 1 . In all low-shot settings, our method VAGER+Voting consistently performs the best in both AUC and F1 metrics. In contrast, LR performs the worst in 1-shot setting, which demonstrates the importance of generalization from base classes when the new class has very few samples. MRN does not work well in most settings, demonstrating that its basic hypothesis that the classiﬁcation parameters trained by large samples and small samples respectively are correlated does not necessarily hold in real data. By comparing VAGER+Voting with the other ﬁve variant versions of our method, we can safely draw the conclusion that the major ingredients in our method, including network embedding for low dimensional representations, mapping function for transforming embedding space to classiﬁcation parameter space, as well as the reﬁnement strategy are necessary and effective and the results support that the Voting strategy performs the best in our sce-

[E3] (text, Section 4.4, page 8): test categories and learn to distinguish these 10 categories on the 1-shot setting. We repeat random selections ﬁve times and the result is shown on the ﬁrst 5 columns in Table 3 . Our VAGER+Voting performs the best in all 5 groups, with promotion of around 2% of average top-1 accuracy, which demonstrates that our method is robust whatever the novel classes are.

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E1 (Section 4.2) states that 'In all low-shot settings, our method VAGER+Voting consistently performs the best in both AUC and F1 metrics.' This exactly matches the claim.

The evidence in E1 (Section 4.2) states that 'LR performs the worst in 1-shot setting, which demonstrates the importance of generalization from base classes when the new class has very few samples.' This exactly matches the claim.

The evidence in E2 (Section Table 2) shows the AUC and F1 scores for the 'Bubble' class under the LR and VAGER methods. The claim states that 'The performance of VAGER is worse than LR for the 'Bubble' class in the 1-shot binary classification setting.' However, the evidence does not provide a direct comparison of the performance of VAGER and LR for the 'Bubble' class. The evidence only shows the AUC and F1 scores for the 'Bubble' class under both methods, which do not directly support the claim.

The evidence in E3 (Section 4.4) states that 'Our VAGER+Voting performs the best in all 5 groups, with promotion of around 2% of average top-1 accuracy, which demonstrates that our method is robust whatever the novel classes are.' This exactly matches the claim.
